clue.text: Page attractive female shortly before dance

indicators.note: shortly asks for the word to be cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a belle is an attractive woman
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: A pageboy turns up just ahead of a dance with a pretty woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel porter who carries luggage and runs errands is a page in American usage.

clue.text: I turn red outside? Rather a different colour

indicators.note: outside says the blushing word goes around the letter I

parts.note: to blush is to turn red in the face

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether going red on the outside means they are changing colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhat blue is a shade other than the red just mentioned, so rather a different colour.

clue.text: Dad's posh car going round river

indicators.note: going round says the car word encircles the father word

parts.note: a limo, short for limousine, is a luxury car
pop is an informal word for a father

explanation.surface: Father's smart limousine drives around a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Limpopo is a major river of southern Africa.

clue.text: Mostly tough customer, finally?

parts.note: hardline means uncompromising, tough in one's position

indicators.note: finally picks out the closing letter of the word customer

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a difficult client has at last arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' signals that the answer, all but its last letter, is HARDLINE for 'tough'; 'finally' supplies the last letter of 'customer'. The whole clue also describes the answer: a tough customer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes an unyielding stance is a tough customer, mostly firm in every position.

clue.text: Enter pastor, revising prayer

indicators.note: revising means the letters of the two words are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A clergyman comes in and edits the service's prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin name for the Lord's Prayer, from its opening words 'Our Father'.

clue.text: Guard colt going west, carrying old Indian

indicators.note: carrying says the turned-round letters hold another letter inside
in an across answer, going west means the pieces read right to left

parts.note: to watch is to guard
C is the abbreviation for colt in horse-racing form

explanation.surface: A Western scene: someone guards a young horse riding west with an elderly Native American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going west' turns WATCH + C into CHCTAW; 'carrying' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Choctaw are a Native American people, called Indians in older usage.

clue.text: Fool with business degree

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a business

explanation.surface: An idiot holds an MBA.
explanation.walkthrough: To cod someone is to fool or hoax them, the sense behind 'codswallop'.
explanation.definitionFit: To kid or hoax someone is to cod them, a British colloquial verb.

clue.text: Single copper is called in at the right moment

indicators.note: a word called in is brought inside, so the metal symbol goes into the number

parts.note: single means one
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A lone police officer is summoned just in time.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor entering on cue comes in exactly at the signal, so at the proper time.

clue.text: Initially, teacher's a little hard on a girl

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of the word teacher's

parts.note: a bit means a little
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A teacher is a little harsh with a schoolgirl.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'on' puts H above A.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabitha is a girl's given name.

clue.text: One getting married after a series of engagements?

definitions.text: One getting married after a series of engagements?

parts.words: One getting married after a series of engagements?
parts.note: engagements reads as several betrothals, but means military battles: a woman who weds a serviceman met during a conflict

explanation.surface: A serial fiancée finally walks down the aisle.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who married a soldier met during wartime, the engagements being battles.

clue.text: Turned me out without tiniest bit of income? That's not deserved

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so the jumble goes round a letter
out signals the letters of the two words are jumbled
the tiniest bit of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone thrown out with no money at all complains it was unfair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the old sense of outside, so the jumble from 'out' wraps the I; a solver may take 'without' as a deletion signal, but nothing is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unmerited has not been earned or justified.

clue.text: Part of trunk displayed in bareback somersaulting

indicators.note: somersaulting means the hidden run is turned backwards
displayed in says the letters are on show within the word bareback

explanation.surface: A circus rider flips over on an unsaddled horse.
explanation.definitionFit: The pole tossed at Highland games is a length cut from a tree trunk.

clue.text: Reportedly unique venue for Olympic Games, once

indicators.note: reportedly says the word is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: sole means one and only, unique

explanation.surface: A news report on a one-off Olympic host city.
explanation.definitionFit: The South Korean capital hosted the 1988 Summer Olympics.

clue.text: It's seen on back of car, I think

definitions.text: It's seen on back of car

explanation.surface: A driver muses about what is on the rear of a car.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads 'I think' as the words of someone who reflects, that is a thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: A red reflecting disc is fitted to a car's rear; and a person who ponders could say 'I think'.

clue.text: Group wanted to liberate political reformer

parts.note: to free is to liberate
a radical seeks sweeping political reform

explanation.surface: A faction campaigns to release a jailed activist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Group' is the chemistry sense: a cluster of atoms with an unpaired electron.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry a reactive atom cluster with an unpaired electron is a group of this kind.

clue.text: Investigation by committee showing great enthusiasm

parts.note: a going-over is a thorough examination
a board is a governing committee

explanation.surface: A committee inquiry goes in with real zeal.
explanation.definitionFit: To go overboard is to be excessively enthusiastic about something.

clue.text: Rector boycotts Brits' party organised in part of church

indicators.note: organised means the remaining letters are arranged anew
a rector who boycotts the event stays away, so his letter is taken out

explanation.surface: A vicar stays away from a British party held in the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boycotts' removes one R from BRITSPARTY; 'organised' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The baptistry is the area of a church where baptisms take place.

clue.text: Mum bringing in potato dish-it's a great success

indicators.note: bringing in says the hush word goes round the potato word

parts.note: keep mum means stay quiet, so mum is shh, the call for silence
mash is mashed potato
the word it, with the 's as a link

explanation.surface: Mother serves mashed potatoes and it's a triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' is not mother but the call for silence, SH.
explanation.definitionFit: A hugely popular song or show is a smash hit.

clue.text: Film review for the under-18s?

parts.note: minority is the state of being under the age of majority
a report is a review

explanation.surface: A cinema critic writes up a movie for teenagers.
explanation.definitionFit: Spielberg's 2002 science-fiction thriller is called this.

clue.text: Successful candidate's one trained to take control of pit

indicators.note: to take control of is to hold, so the jumbled word wraps the pit word
trained means the letters of one are put through new paces into another order

parts.note: a pit is a mine

explanation.surface: The winning applicant was trained to run a colliery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trained' gives NOE, wrapped round the pit by 'to take control of'; 'Successful candidate's' is the definition with 's as is, not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominee is someone named or put forward, here one who has been chosen.

clue.text: East End artist's colourful show

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is an artist; the 's means is
the artist is in Bow, a district of London's East End

explanation.surface: A Cockney painter puts on a vivid exhibition.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'artist is in East End': RA IN BOW. Bow is an area of East London.
explanation.definitionFit: An arc of colours in the sky is nature's colourful show.

clue.text: Get oral invitation to a sale?

indicators.note: oral says the phrase is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: come buy is a trader's call to shoppers

explanation.surface: Someone receives a spoken summons to a sale.
explanation.definitionFit: To come by something is to obtain it.

clue.text: Prime Minister is given backing on stringed instrument by leader of dire pop group

indicators.note: given backing means the two pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: a lyre is an ancient stringed instrument

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A PM endorses a lyre player fronting an awful band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given backing' turns PM IS into SIMP.
explanation.definitionFit: Simply Red is a British band led by Mick Hucknall.

clue.text: Writer translated carol

indicators.note: translated means the word's letters are converted into a new form

explanation.surface: An author puts a Christmas song into another language.
explanation.definitionFit: Federico García Lorca was a Spanish poet and playwright.

clue.text: Fellow of suspect origin? Not right

indicators.note: suspect means the letters are doubtful, so rearranged
not means leave out the letter for right

explanation.surface: A man of dubious background is in the wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' removes R from ORIGIN; 'suspect' rearranges OIGIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Inigo is a man's name, as in the architect Inigo Jones; a fellow is a man.

clue.text: Name of American queen?

explanation.surface: Someone asks what to call a US monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The first is the US spelling of a word for good name or reputation; in bridge the ace, king, queen, jack and ten are the top cards so called.
explanation.definitionFit: A good name is one's reputation, spelt the American way; and a queen is one of the top-ranking court cards in bridge.

clue.text: Emotional wife once read it in telegram

parts.note: an ex is a former wife

indicators.note: in says the word it sits inside the telegram word

parts.note: a cable is a telegram

explanation.surface: A former wife gets upset reading something in a telegram.
explanation.definitionFit: Easily stirred up, highly emotional.

clue.text: City bank fails to open

indicators.note: fails to open means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on

explanation.surface: A city bank does not open for business.
explanation.definitionFit: Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire.

clue.text: The rough, heartless treatment

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter is taken out

parts.note: raspy means rough, grating

explanation.surface: Rough handling with no compassion.
explanation.definitionFit: Therapy is treatment for an illness or disorder.

clue.text: Reserve, first to be excluded from sport on opponents' ground

indicators.note: says the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: play is sport or fun
an away match is played at the other side's ground

explanation.surface: A team lets one player sit out an away fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: Layaway is a scheme for reserving goods with a deposit until fully paid.
